Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today 1 the team found the latency and cost examples helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get to a scoped POC: 

- Goal: Run model fit and quality evals for customer support summarization (shorting support transcripts to 2-3 sentence resolutions) across a few model variants to validate accuracy vs latency/cost.
- What we can provide: ~2k annotated transcripts (CSV), a simple rubric for scoring, and a list of sensitive PII fields to redact.
- Constraints: Data must not persist past the POC (30 days retention), and we need SOC 2 evidence for any infra touching our data.

Can you confirm the required dataset format and what you typically run (automatic metrics vs human eval)? Also curious on recommended model candidates to test on Redwood and a rough timeline (we're hoping for an initial eval within 10 business days).

Attaching a short requirements doc and a tiny sample.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir 1 great to meet you and thanks for the clear recap. Looping in Neha (solutions / POC lead) and Rishi (ML infra) to scope the eval and turn this into an action plan. Quick answers up front: 

- Recommended models to start: redwood/open-instruct-1.5 (baseline), redwood/opt-8q (cost-optimized), and a smaller quantized variant for latency-sensitive slices (we can run both 8-bit and 4-bit if you'd like).
- Metrics: automatic metrics we typically run for summarization are ROUGE-L and BLEU plus exact-match where applicable; we pair that with a small human annotation pass for faithfulness/accuracy (10-20% sample).
- Dataset format: CSV with columns id, prompt, expected_summary, source_text, and optionally metadata tags (channel, priority). We'll give you a sample schema and a small CLI to validate the CSV before upload.
- Security/retention: we support 30-day retention and can enable no-persistence mode for POC runs; SOC 2 evidence and an SCP of required controls can be shared via our security intake flow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Neha will send the eval runner instructions + CSV schema and scoring config.
2) You upload the sample dataset to the Drive link and share any redaction rules.
3) Rishi will kick off an initial run on a small subset (250 examples) to surface latency/cost and quality numbers.
4) We'll sync after initial results and plan the 2-week POC cadence.

Timeline: we can start the initial run as soon as we have the CSV and redaction rules 1 target start within 5 business days, full 2-week POC thereafter.

I'm attaching a short 'eval runner' quickstart as well.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Redwood evals and next steps 1 FinCo POC

Hi Samir 1 thanks for the attachments and clear goals. Adding technical details for the eval setup below (copying in the run templates so you can review):

Dataset CSV schema (required columns):
- id (string) 1 unique identifier
- source_text (string) 1 full support transcript/text to summarize
- prompt (string) 1 the prompt you'd like applied; if blank we'll use our default summarization prompt
- expected_summary (string) 1 golden/reference summary
- channel (optional) 1 web/email/phone

Scoring config:
- Automatic: ROUGE-L (primary), BLEU (secondary), average token-length delta
- Thresholds we recommend to consider model acceptable: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 AND human faithfulness >= 0.85 on sample audit.
- Human eval: we run a blind 3-annotator agreement check on a 10% sample; we'll provide the annotation UI and a short rubric (faithful, concise, misses-critical).

Data handling and PII:
- If the CSV contains PII fields, please mark them in a 'pii_fields' column or provide a separate mapping file; we'll apply your redaction rules before storage.
- For POC runs we can enable 'no-persistence' mode so model input/outputs are not retained in long-term storage.

Eval runner options:
- Quick CLI: redwood-eval run --config finco_eval.yaml --input finco_sample_dataset.csv --output results.json
- Or run via console: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/run/finco-poc (we'll provide a one-time upload link)

Deliverables from our side:
- A results bundle with per-example metrics, aggregated tables, and the human evaluation report.
- A short quality regression check vs your current service (if you provide historical outputs).

Question for you: do you want us to apply model-specific prompt engineering (e.g., turn-level instructions) or keep prompts identical across models? Many customers start with identical prompts to attribute differences to model capacity.

I'll wait for your confirmation on prompt strategy and the redaction list.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
